outcome_detail: U.S. District Judge Elaine Bucklo dismissed all claims against Eddie Johnson and the City of Chicago on March 20, 2024 (Donald v. City of Chicago, No. 1:20-cv-06815, N.D. Ill.), finding the evidence indicated Donald welcomed and actively participated in the relationship. Donald's attorney announced plans to appeal; no appellate ruling or Seventh Circuit docket was located as of July 2026.
criminal_detail: No criminal charges were filed against Eddie Johnson in connection with Donald's allegations. Johnson had earlier been fired as superintendent in December 2019 for making false statements about an unrelated incident in which he was found asleep in his car.
incident_date_approx: 2016-2019, while Donald was assigned to Johnson's security detail
description: Chicago police officer Cynthia Donald, formerly Superintendent Eddie Johnson's driver on his security detail, sued Johnson and the City of Chicago in October 2020 (removed to federal court in November 2020). The suit alleged that between 2016 and 2019 Johnson subjected her to sexual assault and harassment, including forcibly kissing her, coercing sex acts, and sending her nude photos, and that he arranged her assignment to his unit to keep her under his control. It also alleged the City exacerbated a hostile work environment by transferring her away from CPD headquarters after Johnson's ouster. Johnson denied the allegations and maintained the relationship was consensual. On March 20, 2024, a federal judge dismissed all claims without trial, concluding the evidence showed Donald welcomed and actively participated in the relationship; her attorney said she planned to appeal, and no appellate ruling has been reported.
notes: Filed before 2021; included because resolution occurred in window.
